question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: the sources do not say how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed. Law 3.1 sentences (1) and (2) give the testing method (full underhand stroke contacting the shuttle over the back boundary line, hit at an upward angle parallel to the side lines), and Law 3.2 sentence (1) gives the pass criterion (lands not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line, as in Diagram B). Diagram B itself and the ITTO guidance on assessing the test result bear on the question without answering it, so they go in related_sentences.
answer.answer: To test whether a shuttle has the right speed, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line [1], and the shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines [2]. A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line [3]. When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit (strength of shot and trajectory), and whether they were hit from the correct location (over the back line) [4]. The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct [5].

citations.quote: To test a shuttle, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line.
The shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines.
A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line as in Diagram B.

When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit (strength of shot and trajectory), and whether they were hit from the correct location (over the back line) (Law 3).
Shuttle Speed The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct.

answer.answer: A black card means that the offending player or pair is disqualified for misconduct: when the Referee decides to disqualify them, a black card is given to the Umpire [1], who calls “Come here” to the offending player or pair, announces the player’s name followed by “disqualified for misconduct” with a specific explanation of the misconduct [2], and at the same time raises the right hand holding the black card above the Umpire’s head [3].
